note: One block per beat. Beat boundaries in the film land in the silence BETWEEN blocks, so no cut falls mid-sentence. Numbers are spelled out because the engine reads digits unreliably.

f1-thirty-years: You have managed fine for thirty years. That is not in question.
But the customers who found you did not find you the same way twice. The phone book. Then a neighbor. Then a phone. Same business, three different front doors.
One hundred and ninety-nine dollars puts you on the one they use now.
f2-know-where: Your customers know where you are. The ones you already have.
The family that moved onto that street last year does not. They looked on a phone at nine at night, when your sign was dark and your door was locked.
A page answers at nine at night. One hundred and ninety-nine dollars for the first year.
f3-not-technical: You are not technical. You will not need to be.
Nobody who has a website built for them touches the machinery. You answer questions about your own business, the ones only you can answer. We build it, we host it, we keep it running.
One hundred and ninety-nine dollars for the first year. You never open a file.
f4-got-burned: You tried before and you got burned. Let us name the pattern.
You paid up front. You never saw proof. Then the calls stopped. We run it the other way around.
You see three real designs of your own business first, reviewed by a person. Then you decide whether to pay.
f5-too-expensive: A website is too expensive. Here is the whole number.
One hundred and ninety-nine dollars. That is fifty-five cents a day for the first year. One page. One year of hosting. A domain that belongs to you.
After the first year it is nine ninety-nine a month, plus the domain. Business email and maintenance are separate.
f6-retiring: You are close to retiring. Then it matters more, not less.
Whoever buys this business buys what transfers. A domain transfers. A page transfers. Thirty years of people knowing your name does not. That walks out the door with you.
One hundred and ninety-nine dollars leaves something behind.
